summary: The stop was rejected, so I used the remaining interval on the sharpest open point: why the entry-point transfer harness reported 'leadership transfer in progress' while the other two harnesses returned success for the same request. Reading that harness answered it. Its trigger loop calls LeadershipTransfer() and then LeadershipTransferToServer inside the same iteration, discarding the first future without waiting on it, and initiateLeadershipTransfer enqueues each call as a separate request on leadershipTransferCh, so the leader loop takes the automatic request first, picks a voter because pickServer skips non-voters, and answers the explicit request at the in-progress flag while that transfer runs. Three recorded claims therefore had to change: the in-progress error is a refusal keyed to the harness's own preceding request rather than to the target's suffrage, the eight, seven and six leaderless samples plus the extra election round in those receipts cannot be attributed to the non-voter request, and the receipts that actually show admission are the demotion race and the flag probe, which call the explicit form alone and receive success or an empty error while the named member never leads. I replaced those two counterevidence items, rewrote the three-harness limitation to state the identified cause and what remains unmeasured, and appended the source finding to the rationale. The conclusion stays violated with the scoped defect asserted, since the admission claim now rests on the two clean harnesses, and all eight counterevidence items and six limitations are carried forward.
